challenges.title: Filter Completed Orders
challenges.context: Your manager only wants completed orders and two useful columns.
challenges.prompt: Using dataframe df, filter status == 'completed' and return only order_id and revenue.
challenges.explanation: Boolean indexing reduces the dataframe to qualifying rows; a second bracket list selects only the requested columns.

challenges.title: Repair Missing Regions
challenges.context: A small CRM extract has missing region labels. The agreed business rule is to preserve them as Unknown rather than guessing.
challenges.prompt: Use fillna('Unknown') on the region column. Treat the blank example as missing for this guided exercise.
hints: Work on a single Series: df['region'].
Assign the cleaned Series back to df['region'].
challenges.explanation: Explicit missing-value rules are safer than inventing categories. In production, empty strings would normally be normalized to null first.

challenges.title: Revenue by Segment
challenges.context: Finance needs one row per customer segment with total completed revenue.
challenges.prompt: Group df by segment and sum revenue.
hints: This changes the grain from order rows to segment rows.
challenges.explanation: groupby creates one group per segment and aggregation collapses each group to its revenue total.

challenges.title: Find the Top Two Orders
challenges.context: The account team wants the two largest orders for immediate follow-up.
challenges.prompt: Sort revenue descending and return the first two rows with order_id and revenue.
challenges.explanation: Sorting before head ensures the retained records are the largest values, not simply the first physical rows.

challenges.title: Create Conversion Rate
challenges.context: Marketing needs a derived conversion-rate percentage for every channel.
hints: New columns are assigned with df['new_column'] = ...
The rate is conversions divided by clicks.
Multiply the decimal by 100 for a percentage.
challenges.explanation: Vectorized column arithmetic calculates the metric for every row without a Python loop.

challenges.title: Completed Revenue by Region
challenges.context: The CFO wants completed revenue by region, excluding cancelled and refunded records.
challenges.prompt: Filter to completed rows, then group by region and sum revenue.
hints: Apply the status filter before aggregating.
Store the filtered frame or chain the operations.
challenges.explanation: Filtering defines the valid revenue population before aggregation. Reversing or omitting that business rule changes the KPI.
